outcomes.statement: Allocate and propagate an end-to-end deadline through serial and parallel work with response and cleanup reserves.
Prove cancellation stops queued, active, and child work within a declared bound.
Classify retry eligibility and enforce bounded randomized retries using attempt and cost budgets.
Make ambiguous remote outcomes safe using scoped idempotency records, atomic effects, and deduplication retention.
Bound fan-out, pools, tenants, and health traffic with explicit admission, fairness, and overload behavior.
Compare breakers, hedges, partial results, and fail-fast behavior by failure model and useful-work economics.
Diagnose and repair retry storm, pool exhaustion, slowdown, partial response, duplicate effect, and cancellation leak from preserved evidence.
Defend a remote-call policy through user outcomes, security, cost, ownership, exceptions, migration, rollback, and reversal evidence.

resources.title: Deadlines
resources.purpose: Ground deadline and propagation behavior in an explicit RPC contract.
resources.assignment: Read Overview through Deadline Propagation; annotate which behavior the library provides and which cleanup remains application-owned.

resources.title: Cancellation
resources.purpose: Separate a cancellation signal from interruption and cleanup completion.
resources.assignment: Read Overview and client/server cancellation sections; list every loop, queue, and child call in your build that must observe cancellation.

resources.title: HTTP Semantics
resources.author_or_publisher: R. Fielding, M. Nottingham, J. Reschke; IETF
resources.purpose: Scope safe and idempotent request semantics without equating a method name to business deduplication.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 9.2.1–9.2.3 and 10.2.3; classify each independent operation and explain what remains unknown after connection loss.

resources.title: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter
resources.purpose: Connect timeout selection, ambiguous outcomes, retry placement, token budgets, and jitter to operated systems.
resources.assignment: Read the complete article; produce an attempt-amplification tree and identify one policy whose safe value depends on your latency distribution.

resources.title: Addressing Cascading Failures
resources.author_or_publisher: Mike Ulrich and Google SRE contributors
resources.purpose: Relate deadlines, retries, health checks, load shedding, and resource exhaustion to cascading failure.
resources.assignment: Read Retry Cascades, Latency and Deadlines, and Testing for Cascading Failures; map each positive feedback loop to a lab metric and mitigation owner.

resources.title: Metastable Failures in the Wild
resources.author_or_publisher: L. Huang, M. Magnusson, A. Baldini, S. Treichler, M. D. Ernst; USENIX
resources.purpose: Distinguish a temporary trigger from the sustaining effect that prevents recovery.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 1–3 and 6; classify the retry-storm trial's trigger, vulnerable state, sustaining effect, and recovery action.

resources.title: Avoiding Cascading Failures at eBay?
resources.author_or_publisher: Craig Fender, Ravindra Punati; eBay and USENIX Association
resources.purpose: Examine failure containment, traffic shifting, operational ownership, and recovery in a large commerce platform without using it as a capstone answer.
resources.assignment: Watch the presentation or use its audio/slides with Lesson 8; record one containment boundary, one coordination risk, and one migration gate.
